kitDescription: Mana is a Wind AR Attacker who opens every fight with Metal γ, a permanent self ATK ▲58.08% buff that only falls off if an ally dies (which never happens in the sim's fights). While γ is up, every 10 of her normal attacks heals the whole team for a small fraction of her Max HP — a heal that matters mainly because it triggers teammates' on-recovery effects like Crown's. Her second passive, Metal σ, speeds her burst-gauge fill by 70.4% until she spends it: entering a Full Burst while holding σ grants her Attack Damage ▲21.12% and ATK ▲63.36% for 10 seconds and consumes σ, which she re-arms by casting her own burst before that Full Burst ends. She also shaves 0.18s off the charge time of the slowest-charging ally for 10s on each Full Burst entry. Her burst buffs her own Sustained Damage by 52.8% for 10s and lays a 10-second damage-over-time on the boss that ticks 396% of her final ATK every second, with the self-buff amplifying exactly those ticks.

verdictRationale: No undocumented gotchas: all 10 kit lines are FAITHFUL (7) or DOCUMENTED_GAP (3, including both unreachable ally-death lines and the twice-flagged charge-support ⚑). Convergence is strong and mechanical — the S5 blind suite runs 14 PASS + 3 SKIP (the skips being exactly the driver's documented gap set) against the shipped override, and the S6 blind independently built the same σ resource-pool economy, the load-bearing centerpiece S2b's spec demanded. The single blind-vs-driver divergence (σ regain at burstCast vs fullBurstEnd) is a genuine kit-text timing ambiguity, self-flagged by the blind as off-by-one-cycle, documented by the driver, and behaviorally pinned where it matters (regain-removal collapses procs to FB1-only). The driver's tests discriminate on every load-bearing line (three-way trigger identity on the FB buffs, counterfactuals on γ timing/scope, DoT magnitude/interval, heal-tandem isolation, regain collapse); the only presence-only pin is the σ gauge passive, which the driver honestly reports as cadence-inert for a 40s-CD unit — that is the maximum discrimination available, not evasion. Same-model residuals the owner should spot-check: (1) the σ regain timing on rotations mana skips (needs a popup/rotation read, both agents are guessing from the same prose); (2) the chargeSpeedPct-18 magnitude, which is exact only for helm's 1.0s base charge and comp-dependent; (3) S2b's stale 'DoT crit OFF' remark — the engine default DOT_CRIT=ON applies and neither implementation overrides it, so behavior is correct, but the spec document itself carries an outdated prior. Ship it.
